newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus banks ponder central bank rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus banks ponder central bank rate cut.

text.p: Cypriot banks kept a 'wait and see' approach on Friday on the likelihood of an interest rate cut after the central bank made the first move by reducing its own deposit and lending rates to commercial banks on Thursday.
The move is widely seen as the central bank's go-ahead to commercial banks to lower its own rates to the public without the need for a special directive.
Effective Friday, the central bank cut its lombard lending rate by half a percentage point to 7.0 percent and cut its overnight deposit rate to 4.0 percent from 5.0 percent.

The central bank expects commercial banks to follow suit with reductions in their retail rates, now 8.5 percent for loans and 7.0 percent for deposits, central bank governor Afxentis Afxentiou said on Thursday.
Group Chief Executive of the Cyprus Popular Bank Kikis Lazarides said the central bank rate changes do not have an effect on retail rates.
"Changes of the interest rates at which we make business with the central bank to cover our transactions have no effect or impact on the other interest rate structure," he told Reuters.

"The interest rate structure here is decided as far as the ceiling is concerned by law at nine percent. The interest rate is decided by the central bank with directives to the commercial banks," said Lazarides.
Commercial banks will lose money with the one percentage point cut in the overnight deposit rate. And the market is so liquid that banks at present need not resort to the Lombard facility, he said.

"The overall position of the economy is liquid so neither will the banks resort to the central bank for borrowing," said Lazarides. "The change in the lombard rate will not affect us, while at the same time we have to keep high (overnight deposit) balances with the central bank because the demand for credit is not there."
Agni Iakovidou of the Programming Department in the Bank of Cyprus said the bank would examine the changes brought about by the central bank. "Soon the bank shall form a view," she said.
Marios Clerides of Hellenic Bank said he expected banks to wait a while before taking any steps in relation to their interest rates.
"The central bank has conveyed a message, a rather strong one, that it wants the interest rates lowered," said Clerides, head of the Economic Research Department in the Bank.
"We will wait a while longer to see how the market moves."
